gaps.sentence: Insure the camera ___ it gets damaged in transit.
gaps.explanation: 'In case it gets damaged' = as a precaution against damage.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: He passed the oral exam ___ the fact that he had barely revised.
gaps.explanation: 'The fact that' turns the clause into a noun phrase, which 'despite' requires.

gaps.sentence: The rehearsals ran late; ___, the premiere itself went off without a hitch.
gaps.explanation: 'Nevertheless' = in spite of what was just said.

gaps.sentence: Demand for the vaccine soared; ___, production was doubled.
gaps.explanation: Soaring demand led to increased production: consequently marks the result.

gaps.sentence: ___ you finish early, come and give us a hand.
gaps.explanation: 'If' introduces a real condition; 'in case' would change the meaning to precaution.

gaps.sentence: ___ his age, he still plays football every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite his age' — noun phrase after despite.
